before.stem: Trace this declared six-slot GA generation. The selected parents are P1,P2,P3,P4,P4,P6, paired (P1,P3),(P4,P6),(P2,P4); swap the second waypoint in each pair, label children C1…C6 in that order, then change only C1 from [(0,3),(3,4)] to C1′=[(0,3),(3,5)]. Use the source grid and H-then-V decoder with C=L+10N_obs+N_turn and F=1/(1+C). Retain old elite P1 in one slot, then the five lowest-cost evaluated children, breaking equal costs by child number. Which child-cost vector, next population and best fitness result?

citations.locator: Lecture L42, physical PDF page 1309, printed footer 13: H-then-V decoding convention.
citations.evidenceText:
Path Decoding
•  To evaluate a chromosome, decode it into a full path. On a grid,
  the segment between two consecutive points can be generated in
   either of these ways:
   – Straight-line segment with collision checking on crossed grid cells.
   – Manhattan routing, moving row/column steps between consecutive points.
• We will use Manhattan segment decoding: move horizontally
    first, then vertically.
•  This turns waypoint chromosomes into explicit
   grid paths that can be checked for obstacle
   collision.


                                                                                                          13

Fitness Function

• A standard GA path-planning fitness is based on inverse path
   length, often with penalties for infeasible paths. One practical
   fitness is:
•  Cost = 𝐿+    +           𝛼𝑁obs  𝛽𝑁turn
•  where:
• 𝐿 = total path length,
•      = number of obstacle violations,  𝑁obs
•       = number of turns, if smoothness matters,  𝑁turn
•  𝛼, 𝛽 are penalty weights.

Lecture L42, physical PDF page 1326, printed footer 30: Pseudocode evaluates candidates and retains an elite; exact fixed-size policy is supplied in this exercise.
citations.evidenceText:
Pseudocode
Input: 6x6 grid, start S, goal G, obstacle set Obs
Output: best path
Initialize population P with N chromosomes
Each chromosome = [W1, W2], where W1 and W2 are free cells
For gen = 1 to MaxGen:
  For each chromosome C in P:
    Decode path: S -> W1 -> W2 -> G
   Compute path length L
    Count obstacle violations Nobs
    Count turns Nturn
    Cost = L + alpha*Nobs + beta*Nturn
     Fitness = 1 / (1 + Cost)
  Keep best chromosome (elitism)
  Select parent pairs from P based on fitness
  For each pair:
    Perform crossover to create children
    Mutate waypoint genes with probability pm
    Repair invalid waypoints if needed
   Add children to new population
  Replace old population with new population
Return chromosome with highest fitness
Decode it into final path

solution.justification: After the specified variation, the six child costs are11,11,23,33,44,33. The fixed-size elite policy retains P1 and all children except C5, so the best evaluated fitness remains1/12. The policy and deterministic tie-break are added exercise conventions, not an assertion that the source ran this exact implementation.

optionExplanations.o1: These costs omit the specified C1 mutation, leaving its cost23 instead of11; the selected set therefore refers to the wrong generation.
optionExplanations.o2: The costs are correct, but the elite plus all six children creates seven slots instead of the required six.
optionExplanations.o3: Evaluate after mutation, retain elite P1, and keep the five lowest-cost children; only C5 with cost44 is dropped.
optionExplanations.o4: The list retains the worst child C5 and omits one best child C2, violating the stated best-five-child policy.
